C1.1.1.q: A hospital wants full control over where patient records are stored and who can reach them, and will pay extra for it. Which cloud model suits it best?
C1.1.1.why: Private cloud is used by one organisation only, giving the most control and security for sensitive data, at a higher cost.

C1.1.1.q: Which is the main DRAWBACK of a private cloud compared with a public cloud?
options: Data is shared with other organisations
It cannot be scaled at all
C1.1.1.why: The organisation must buy, house and maintain its own servers and staff to run them.

C1.1.2.q: A new start-up has little money and expects users to grow quickly. It wants to pay only for what it uses. Which cloud model should it choose?
C1.1.2.why: Public cloud is pay-as-you-go and scales easily, so it suits small organisations with changing demand.

C1.1.2.q: A school uses Microsoft 365, run on servers shared by thousands of other organisations. What is a risk of this model?
options: Less control over where its data is physically stored
It can only be used on-site
C1.1.2.why: In a public cloud the provider controls the hardware and data location, so the school has less control.

C1.1.3.q: A retailer keeps card payment data on its own servers but runs its busy website on AWS so it can cope with Black Friday traffic. Which model is this?
C1.1.3.why: Hybrid cloud mixes private (sensitive data) and public (scalable, cheaper workloads).

C1.1.4.q: A games company rents virtual servers from Azure. Its own staff install the operating system and the game server software. Which service model is this?
C1.1.4.why: With IaaS the provider supplies the hardware; the customer manages the OS and software.

C1.1.5.q: A small accountancy firm pays a monthly fee per user for Google Workspace. The provider handles all updates, servers and security. Which service model is this?
C1.1.5.why: SaaS delivers finished software over the internet; the provider manages everything.

C1.1.6.q: A team of developers wants to build and launch a web app without having to set up or manage any servers or operating systems. Which service model should they use?
C1.1.6.why: PaaS gives developers a ready-made platform to build and deploy apps on.

C1.2.q: A business replaces its own server room with cloud services. Which is a likely impact?
options: IT costs move from large up-front purchases to ongoing subscriptions
Staff can no longer work from home
It no longer needs an internet connection
Its data can never be lost
C1.2.why: Cloud turns capital spending on hardware into a regular running cost, and depends on internet access.

C1.2.q: Which is a disadvantage of an organisation relying on cloud computing?
options: Services stop if the internet connection fails
Data cannot be shared between staff
It must buy extra servers every year
C1.2.why: Cloud services are reached over the internet, so poor connectivity stops work.

C1.3.1.q: Staff working from home need to reach the company's internal file server securely over their home broadband. What should the company provide?
C1.3.1.why: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel over the internet into the organisation's network.

C1.3.2.q: An IT technician in head office takes control of a branch employee's PC to fix a settings problem without travelling. What technology are they using?
C1.3.2.why: Remote desktop software lets one computer view and control another computer's desktop over a network.

C1.4.1.q: A bank is choosing an online system. Its top concern is that customer data is encrypted and that the system meets UK GDPR. Which selection factor is this?
C1.4.1.why: Security covers encryption, access control and legal compliance.

C1.4.2.q: A charity compares systems by adding up subscription fees, staff training and the effort of moving its old data across. Which factor is it judging?
C1.4.2.why: Cost includes subscriptions, data transfer, training and migration, not just the price tag.

C1.4.3.q: A care home's staff have limited IT skills, so the manager wants a rota system they can learn in a few minutes. Which factor matters most?
C1.4.3.why: Ease of use is how quickly staff and customers can learn and use the system.

C1.4.4.q: A dentist rejects an online booking system because it cannot send text reminders, which the practice needs. Which factor caused the rejection?
C1.4.4.why: Features means whether the system's functions match what the organisation actually needs.

C1.4.5.q: A farm in a rural area with slow, unreliable broadband is unsure whether to move to cloud software. Which factor is the main worry?
C1.4.5.why: Online systems depend on the quality and reliability of the internet connection.

C1.4.6.q: An online shop gets ten times more visitors at Christmas and wants extra capacity just for December. Which factor should it look for in a system?
C1.4.6.why: Scalability is the ability to increase or reduce capacity as demand changes, without major cost or disruption.

C2.1.1.q: A clothing brand wants to share photos and short videos of new products and let customers like, comment and share them. Which online community should it use?
C2.1.1.why: Social media platforms let users create, share and interact with content.

C2.1.2.q: A tech reviewer posts regular video reviews of new phones on YouTube. What is this an example of?
C2.1.2.why: A vlog is the video version of a blog: regularly updated content from one creator.

C2.1.3.q: A company wants a knowledge base that any member of staff can add to and edit, so procedures stay up to date. What should it set up?
C2.1.3.why: A wiki is a website that many users can create and edit together.

C2.1.4.q: A gaming community wants a space where many members can type to each other live at the same time in themed rooms. Which tool fits?
C2.1.4.why: Chatrooms let several users talk in real time by text.

C2.1.5.q: A manager wants to send quick real-time text messages to one colleague or a small project team during the day. Which tool fits best?
C2.1.5.why: Instant messaging is real-time text chat between individuals or small groups, e.g. WhatsApp or Teams.

C2.1.6.q: A college records weekly audio revision episodes that students can download and listen to on the bus. What is this?
C2.1.6.why: Podcasts are audio episodes published online to listen to on demand.

C2.1.7.q: A software company wants customers to post questions and reply to each other in threads, which others can read and answer later. Which tool should it use?
C2.1.7.why: Forums are discussion boards with threads that users post to in their own time, not live.

C2.2.1.q: Users complain that a council's community app is slow to load and hard to use with a screen reader. Which consideration does this affect?
C2.2.1.why: UX covers how easy, fast, available and accessible the platform is.

C2.2.2.q: A youth club chooses a platform with group video calls because its members asked for them. Which consideration is it addressing?
C2.2.2.why: Meeting user needs means the platform's features match what its users actually need.

C2.2.3.q: A small business finds that running an online community needs paid hosting and a part-time moderator. Which consideration is this?
C2.2.3.why: Cost covers subscriptions, hosting, moderation and staff.

C2.2.4.q: Members are worried that a forum sells their email addresses to advertisers. Which consideration is this?
C2.2.4.why: Privacy is about how personal data is protected and whether it is shared with third parties.

C2.2.5.q: Hackers take over several accounts on a company's social media page and post malicious links. Which consideration failed?
C2.2.5.why: Security protects accounts and data on the platform from hacking and malicious content.

C2.2.6.q: A company's Teams service goes offline for four hours, so staff cannot talk to customers. Which consideration is this?
C2.2.6.why: Downtime is time when the platform is unavailable, so users cannot communicate.

C2.2.7.q: Older staff struggle to post on the new company intranet until they attend a short workshop. Which consideration does this show?
C2.2.7.why: Staff and users may need training to use and manage a platform well.

C2.2.8.q: A firm chooses Microsoft Teams because it links straight into the Outlook calendars and SharePoint files it already uses. Which consideration is this?
C2.2.8.why: Integration is how easily the platform connects to systems the organisation already uses.

C2.2.9.q: A manager notices staff spend hours scrolling the company social feed instead of finishing tasks. Which consideration is affected?
C2.2.9.why: Online communities can raise or lower how much staff get done.

C2.2.10.q: A company writes rules banning staff from posting confidential information or abusing customers on social media. What is this an example of?
C2.2.10.why: Organisations set policies, such as an AUP, for how staff behave on online communities.
